name: Hilkiah
overview: Hilkiah is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Eliakim, as noted in 2 Kings 18:18. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him in Scripture. His mention is brief but establishes a familial connection important for understanding certain biblical lineages.
namesAndTitles: The name Hilkiah means 'YHWH is [my] portion,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that highlights reliance on the Lord. This proper name, recorded in 2 Kings 18:18, does not indicate any title but conveys a personal devotion to God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hilkiah as the father of Eliakim, as stated in 2 Kings 18:18. Beyond this, there are no other family relationships noted, and no further familial details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hilkiah's significance lies in his role as the father of Eliakim, which situates him within the genealogical and historical context of the biblical narrative. Though his personal story is not elaborated, his mention connects to the broader unfolding of God's providential plan through the generations recorded in Scripture. This connection underscores the importance of family lines in God's redemptive history.
